column3: specific outstanding behavior (proposals remain in the denominator)
The native handler stack has an exception value, but no sys.exc_info tuple API. Returning a constant triple outside handlers would leave active-handler semantics wrong.
The tuple must identify the ValueError type, the caught ValueError(42) object, and that object's actual traceback.
Raising the exception class must preserve the caught instance, its runtime type and traceback across sys.exc_info().
Native handler identity works; compiling the unchanged body also requires ValueError(42) and passing ValueError as a class value to assertIsInstance (#501, #508).
The complete native body passes the real ValueError class to assertIsInstance before checking identity; that class operand is unsupported (#501, #508).
Assigning a Python callable to sys.displayhook must affect eval of code compiled in single mode.
The hook must hold the active output stream while an object's __repr__ replaces sys.stdout and forces collection.
Deleting the displayhook must cause single-mode eval to raise RuntimeError; neither mutable sys hooks nor single-mode eval exist.
The native default hook must write to a swappable stdout, update builtins._, ignore None, and report a deleted stdout.
Calling the default hook with invalid exception data must route an unraisable diagnostic to a captured stderr.
Rendering a SyntaxError with a bytes filename needs structured exception args, line data and a replaceable stderr.
Formatted frames, sys.exc_info unpacking, and the callable original hook must work in the captured-stderr fixture.
Callable identities must survive get/set, invalid setters must leave both hooks untouched, and async generators must consult those hooks.
Writing a shutdown diagnostic must retain the stream even when its write method removes the last sys.stderr reference.
Both assertions require CPython's variable PyObject header plus one PyLong digit for True, including getsizeof(True, -1). Imre uses a tagged bool; only those byte counts are proposed.
getsizeof must invoke user __sizeof__, propagate exceptions, return the caller's sentinel, and reject overflow. The separate CPython GC-header arithmetic does not exempt these behaviors.
The two exact sizes use _testinternalcapi.SIZEOF_PYGC_HEAD, CPython PyVarObject headers and digit size; those headers do not exist on Imre bools/lists.
The assertions enumerate exact C struct sizes for Objects/ types, including pointers, PyLong digits and CPython Unicode caches. Imre uses different layouts; ordinary getsizeof stays open.
The _ast.AST, traceback and sys.flags byte sizes are calculated from CPython C pointer layouts and struct-sequence fields; those expressions do not specify Imre object sizes.
This test derives subclass sizes from CPython's three additional slot pointers and, when needed, the GC header, including an additional GC header relative to the base object.
This single routine also reads float_info, int_info, hash_info, prefixes, builtin names and implementation metadata. Hash and digit descriptions need to agree with actual native algorithms.
The native child needs per-stream error policies under LC_ALL=C, PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0, -X utf8=0 and PYTHONIOENCODING overrides.
sys.call_tracing must accept a real callable and tuple and reject the non-tuple argument. The native tracing/callable boundary is absent.
The sole call is deprecated sys._clear_type_cache(), whose warning refers to CPython's method lookup cache. Imre statically resolves methods; this proposes only this private cache warning.
The sys snapshot must associate each running thread with its active exception; a current-thread TLS value alone cannot satisfy the two-thread fixture.
Requires a live frame snapshot for a blocked second thread, its f_back chain and code names. No Python-visible native frame registry exists.
The stderr assertions name pymalloc arenas and the free PyDictObjects list. Imre does not use those CPython allocators or freelists.
This sole assertion ties the CPython extension ABI suffix 't' to its Py_GIL_DISABLED configure flag. Imre does not implement that binary extension ABI.
A persistent native loader policy must be shared by get/setdlopenflags and future extension loading, with errors for invalid arity.
Imre currently returns the host helper interpreter; the original also relaunches with overridden argv[0], executable and PATH. A host Python child cannot validate the native boundary (#302).
The unchanged method verifies the native caught payloads and child exits through stderr flushing. Compiling its next child with lone U+DCFF fails before the final Latin-1 check (#405, #409).
Requires interactive stdin/REPL execution and exit propagation from exit(), __import__('sys').exit and raise SystemExit for statuses 0 and 123.
The check uses live allocation counts before and after gc.collect, with optional total refcount/intern accounting. The native allocator does not expose these counters.
A callable native frame must expose the test function's actual code object by identity and reject out-of-range depth and extra arguments.

Native source frames supply the current or calling module and return None beyond the stack. The original first comparison still needs unittest equality for str | None; its loop needs sys._getframe, f_globals and f_back identity.
Public PEP 421 fields need an actual Imre version, named version tuple, cache policy and isolation capabilities. A local implementation is being aligned with the shared named-tuple layout (#497).

The original parent can query one live native string table. The whole native body also needs its test.support/random imports, callable assertions and the original local str subclass S with its own __hash__.
The native streams must honor CP424, ASCII replacement/strict/surrogateescape, and emit Python UnicodeEncodeError for unencodable writes.
The runtime must transition during final destruction, after atexit; the original reads sys.is_finalizing both during execution and inside __del__.
The reference predicate is configured by CPython's build. The native thread model must supply an honest GIL capability; the host build flag is not target evidence.
Original child reads and prints sys.flags and sys.float_info from __del__ during shutdown; native destruction must keep both usable.
The runtime needs an immutable frozenset of its standard library module names and iterable native string elements.
The static module loader does not expose Python's mutable meta_path or its initialized finder instances.
The same verified child checks stdin/stdout/stderr error policies under LC_ALL=POSIX, both with and without an encoding override.
Repeated genuine native recursive calls must raise RecursionError at each configured depth and recover for the next depth.
Native getrefcount must reject missing arguments, preserve the None singleton count across global bindings and expose total count only if available.
Rejecting a limit below the current depth needs actual frame depth and exception-safe restoration of nested calls.
The target directory must agree with the target os module's file origin; a CPython installation path is not a native standard library.
The asserted addresses of dynamically interned strings must differ across CPython subinterpreters. Imre lacks isolated interpreters; public sys.intern remains open.
The assertions require shared zero- and one-character Latin-1 singleton addresses across CPython interpreters, including a private _is_interned result.
The fixture compares process addresses for CPython's Tools/build/generate_global_objects.py string list across interpreters. Imre has no equivalent generated table.
Requires persistent get/set of a real thread switch interval, floating-point round trips, and invalid type/value checks.
Read actual launch flags by 18 dynamic attribute names, preserve their bool/int types, and expose struct-sequence length and representation.
The flags value and its type must exist, and Python-level construction of that type must be rejected.
Storing a user object on sys and finalizing its failing destructor quietly needs mutable module attributes and native shutdown ownership.
Real chained native frames must be formatted or suppressed according to mutable sys.tracebacklimit on uncaught errors.
Needs a real version-info type object and its construction error, in addition to exposed tuple fields and indexing.
Each injected script must run in a new globals dictionary distinct from the target's __main__.__dict__.
Inject and execute the actual script at a safe point in the waiting target; no native debugger transport exists.
The same cross-process operation must accept a bytes path without involving a CPython child.
The target must honor PYTHON_DISABLE_REMOTE_DEBUG=1 and report its disabled state to the caller.
The target must honor -Xdisable-remote-debug and the injector must report that policy; command-line flags and transport are prerequisites.
Starting the caller itself with the disabling environment variable must prevent remote_exec before it reaches the target.
Starting the caller with -Xdisable-remote-debug must prevent its remote_exec operation.
Native remote_exec must validate a nonexistent target PID and raise OSError.
Native remote_exec must reject None and integer script values with TypeError before transport.
Calling remote_exec on the current PID with a nonexistent script path must produce OSError.
Deliver the event and its actual script path to the target's audit hook while the injected script runs.
An invalid remote script must produce SyntaxError in the target without killing its process or printing script output.
The debugger and native filesystem/argv string domain must preserve a filename containing undecodable bytes.
An exception in injected code must be reported by the target main thread while its process continues.
The current native process must schedule its own script and observe its output at a safe point.

The child imports _testinternalcapi.TIER2_THRESHOLD and _testcapi.pyobject_vectorcall to assert CPython tier transitions around C and inlined frames. This proposal applies to these two private CPython APIs; Imre exposes the JIT capability of its own compilation mode.
The native hook must receive the original error, exception type, traceback, offending object and formatted message. The unchanged trigger uses _testcapi.err_writeunraisable/err_formatunraisable.
Reporting failure of the user's hook needs the actual hook repr and traceback; its input is produced via _testcapi.err_writeunraisable.
The default hook must write real diagnostics from the _testcapi.err_writeunraisable/err_formatunraisable fixture, preserving offending object and traceback.
A failing __del__ must route exceptions to the actual retained stderr even when the exception's __str__ fails.
A _testcapi.err_writeunraisable trigger must print a nested exception's qualname and selectively omit the builtins or __main__ module prefix.
Calling sys.__unraisablehook__ with an arbitrary object must raise TypeError; no original native unraisable hook exists yet.
